newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn says German hostages in Yemen still well.
newsitem.headline: Bonn says German hostages in Yemen still well.

text.p: The Bonn Foreign Ministry said on Wednesday four German tourists kidnapped by mountain tribesmen in Yemen's rugged interior were still well, according to letters from them received by the German embassy in Sanaa.

"As far as we know the state of the hostages is good. We know this from two letters received by our embassy in Yemen yesterday or the day before from the hostages," a foreign ministry spokesman told a news conference.
But the spokesman said he could not confirm German media reports that the hostage takers wanted a ransom of five million marks ($3 million) for the release of the tourists.
"The particular motives and demands of the hostage takers are still unclear," he said.

The hostages -- two men and two women -- were abducted last Thursday while returning to the capital Sanaa from the eastern Marib governorate. The kidnappings came less than a month after tribesmen released seven German motorcycle tourists after more than week in captivity in the southeastern Hadramaut province.

An official source said on Monday Yemeni security forces were maintaining a cordon around the kidnappers and negotiations were continuing but authorities would not yield to any demands by the kidnappers.
Germany has set up crisis centres in Bonn and at the German embassy in Sanaa to deal with the latest kidnapping.

In recent years, Yemeni tribes with grievances against the government or foreign oil firms have kidnapped scores of tourists, diplomats and other foreigners to use as bargaining chips. The demands have rarely been political and tended to involve land or water disputes.
The hostages have all been released unharmed.

Marib has been the site of previous hostage takings. A U.S. engineer kidnapped by Yemeni tribemen in Marib was released in February after 16 days in captivity. A French diplomat was also kidnapped in Marib in October and set free two weeks later.
